clue.text: City where treasure may be stored by bishop, say, and Queen

parts.note: a bishop is one example of a chessman, a MAN on the board
treasure is classically kept in a chest
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: A tour of a city's bank vaults, overseen by a bishop and the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bishop, say' reads as a churchman, but it is one example of a chess piece; chess sets are also called chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester is a major city in north-west England.

clue.text: Bouquet for tech owner who added 'X' on …

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a scent or fragrance
second meaning: Elon ..., who bought Twitter and renamed it X

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs the surface on into the next clue; 'Bouquet' is a perfume, not flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Musk is a strong animal scent used in perfumery, and also the surname of the businessman who rebranded Twitter as X.

clue.text: .. bid to ban candidate?

parts.note: NO as in 'no smoking', a prohibition
Donald Trump, a presidential candidate

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a proposal to bar a particular politician from standing.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, a no-trump bid is a call to play the hand with no trump suit.
explanation.definitionFit: No-trump is a call in the card game bridge, so it is a kind of bid.

clue.text: Goal-fest at Everton … could be this home ground!

definitions.text: Goal-fest at Everton … could be this home ground!

parts.words: Goal-fest at Everton … could be this home ground!
parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: the phrase 'Goal-fest at Everton' is literally housing the word estate across its letters, and the answer is also a kind of residential ground

explanation.surface: A high-scoring match at Everton's stadium, celebrated as a home win.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is self-referential: look inside 'fest at Everton' and the six letters ESTATE are housed there, so the phrase is a HOUSING ESTATE. 'home ground' confirms the meaning: Everton is a Liverpool football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A housing estate is an area of ground built up with homes, so it is literally home ground.

clue.text: Engineer leaves the Spanish geographer's base

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rearrange, so the letters of leaves are rebuilt

parts.note: EL is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish geographer's base camp is rigged up by someone who then departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Geographers measure heights from mean sea level, the zero baseline for altitude.

clue.text: He'd blog regularly — pretty good work on screen

indicators.note: taking every other letter at even intervals through the words He'd blog

parts.note: OK means passable, fairly good

explanation.surface: A blogger writes so-so posts that make a decent read online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of HEDBLOG, giving EBO.
explanation.definitionFit: An e-book is a written work read on an electronic display rather than paper.

clue.text: Clock set to go backwards

indicators.note: the word for set is read from its end to its start

parts.note: laid, as in set down or put in place

explanation.surface: Instructions for putting the clocks back at the end of summer time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clock' is slang for face, and so is dial.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for a person's face, so each can stand for the other.

clue.text: Local alcohol delivered for member of the club

indicators.note: delivered as in spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a local is British for one's nearby pub, an inn; cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples

explanation.surface: A pub's own drink is brought round to a club member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British for one's nearby pub, an inn; said out loud, INN CIDER matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider is someone within a group or organisation, privy to its affairs.

clue.text: Eleventh-hour stay, little to the south

indicators.note: in a down entry, south means below, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: to last is to endure or remain
minute means tiny

explanation.surface: A late-booked holiday stay, going south.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean happening at the latest possible moment, just before a deadline.

clue.text: Food devoured by hippopotamus tastes revolting

indicators.note: revolting says the hidden letters are read backwards
the answer is swallowed inside the hippo's words, as if eaten by it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hippo finds some food disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Food devoured' as the definition, but 'devoured by' is what signals the hidden letters, leaving 'Food' alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a type of small citrus fruit, something eaten.

clue.text: Universe having no origin is absorbing

indicators.note: the first letter, where the word begins, is dropped

parts.note: the cosmos is the universe

explanation.surface: A cosmological puzzle: a universe without a beginning is captivating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no origin' drops C from COSMOS, leaving OSMOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is the gradual soaking up of fluid through a membrane, a process of taking in.

clue.text: Families may be putting in this reduced model of course

definitions.text: Families may be putting in this
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a game families play, putting being the short golf stroke
second meaning: a scaled-down version of a golf course

explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' reads as 'placing', and 'of course' as 'naturally'; both are golf here.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazy golf or minigolf is played with a putter on small novelty holes, a shrunken golf course.

clue.text: Team from 1 Across land here?

parts.note: Manchester United, the football club, known simply as United
a kingdom is a realm or land

explanation.surface: Asking whether a football team from Manchester would arrive in this country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' points to where the Daily Telegraph is published, Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Telegraph is a British paper, so for its readers this country is home.

clue.text: Feline — Matisse fancifully captures one that's played up

indicators.note: the jumbled name holds the other piece inside it
fanciful means imaginative, so the painter's name is reworked
up, in a down entry, reads the card bottom to top

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A Matisse painting imaginatively depicts a cat and a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' works because this is a down entry: the card's letters are read from the bottom of the light upwards before going inside the jumbled painter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Siamese is a breed of domestic cat from Thailand, so it is a kind of feline.

clue.text: Denounced cryptic e.g. with dim pun

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or puzzling, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A setter is criticised for a weak pun in a cryptic clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn is to challenge or attack as false, so denounced matches in the past tense.

clue.text: A river bordered by bird burrows

indicators.note: the first pieces have the bird on either side of them

parts.note: a wren is a small bird
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A riverbank lined with birds and animal holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A warren is a network of interconnecting rabbit holes, a set of underground tunnels.

clue.text: Pass on portion of sweet, a gel Edward flipped over

indicators.note: flipped over says the hidden letters are read backwards
a portion is a part, so the answer is a stretch inside these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Sharing a piece of a jelly sweet with Edward, who turns it over.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft folded 'portion' into the definition, but 'portion of' is what signals the hidden letters; 'Pass on' alone defines the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To delegate is to hand a task or responsibility down to someone else.

clue.text: Growth of passion — 'Mail me back' getting oddly ignored

indicators.note: the kept letters are then read from right to left
the first, third, fifth letters and so on are skipped, keeping only the even ones

explanation.surface: A passionate lover asks to be written to in return.
explanation.walkthrough: Keeping the even letters of PASSIONMAILME gives ASOMIM, and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa is a flowering shrub or tree, a plant that grows.

clue.text: Number whose abbreviation would be its square root in Rome

definitions.text: Number whose abbreviation would be its square root in Rome

parts.words: Number whose abbreviation would be its square root in Rome
parts.note: the number is abbreviated M, and in Roman numerals M means a thousand, which multiplied by itself gives the number

explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation is M; as a Roman numeral M is 1,000, and 1,000 squared is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A million is one thousand times one thousand, so a thousand is its square root.

clue.text: 'Ratty — Favourite Little Creature' university student's penned

indicators.note: penned as in shut in a pen, so the pieces are enclosed

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
an ant is a tiny insect
L is a learner, as on British L-plates for learner drivers

explanation.surface: Reads like a title of a student's story about a rat, Ratty from The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ratty' looks like the character from The Wind in the Willows, but here it means irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for bad-tempered, and petulant means sulky and irritable.

clue.text: Self-built small ground-level home, not flat

definitions.text: Self-built small ground-level home, not flat

parts.words: Self-built small ground-level home, not flat
parts.note: insects build their own mound of earth on the ground; it is a small hill, so it is not flat, nor a flat in the housing sense

explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment, but it means level: this home is a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthill is a mound of soil built by ants as their nest.

clue.text: Lower chamber standing behind represented false humility

indicators.note: this piece comes after the anagram
re-presented, shown again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a basement is the room below ground level

explanation.surface: Parliament's lower house backs a misleading show of modesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower chamber' suggests the House of Commons; it is a basement. FALSE rearranged gives SELFA.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-abasement is belittling oneself, an excessive or showy form of humility.

clue.text: Field that takes an age to turn over

indicators.note: in a down entry the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: an era is an age

explanation.surface: A pasture that takes forever to plough.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a sphere of activity, as in the field of politics.

clue.text: Imprisons writers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as in shuts in an enclosure

explanation.walkthrough: 'writers' looks like authors; it means instruments for writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for confining animals and a plural noun for ink writing tools.

clue.text: What might lead to whispers from Wuhan?

definitions.text: What might lead to whispers from Wuhan?

parts.words: What might lead to whispers from Wuhan?
parts.note: the party game is called by this word followed by whispers, and something from Wuhan is from China

explanation.walkthrough: Chinese whispers is a game where a message is passed along a line and garbled; Wuhan is a city in China.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means from China, the country where Wuhan is, and it precedes whispers in the game's name.

clue.text: Oxygen contributes to exercising easing stress

indicators.note: exercising works the letters over, putting them into a new order

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Breathing in oxygen during exercise helps reduce stress.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to worry or fret intensely over something.

clue.text: This could be canned music — no energy, but it has a following

indicators.note: the A is placed after the shortened word
no says the energy letter is left out

parts.note: a tune is a piece of music
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Canned music, piped through speakers, still has its fans despite its lack of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canned music' is misleading: 'This could be canned' is the definition. 'no energy' takes E from TUNE, and 'it has a following' adds A after.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a fish commonly sold preserved in tins.

clue.text: They rush over after wall's destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed means smashed up, so the letters are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A flood surges through once a wall collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterfalls are cascades of water pouring over a drop.
